pr_title: Fix transit-only resupply stuck loop and force fire pathing
pr_body:
fix #17889

* Attacking whilst pathing over transit tiles prevents unit from stopping on a transit tile.
* Move orders can be cancelled on a transit-only tile.
* Idling on a transit only tile causes the unit to move away if it can.

This has potential to introduce regressions that relied on Move not being able to be cancelled on a transit-only tile unless it was marked as destination, although I'm not sure that destination tiles can be transit-only from regular move orders.
pr_comments:
> The issue that units can become uncontrollable technically still exists but it's not an issue for default mods. See gif below for an example that they can become uncontrollable when ordered to occupied cells that are surrounded by transit-only tiles.

@matjaeck Yes, we decided not to fix this because the solutions we discussed are far more likely to cause other unknown issues. It would need to be fixed in an early playtest rather than a late playtest/release candidate.

issue_context.title: SD "O" cell (passable but not stoppable) - Unit still can idle on those cells. (
issue_context.body:
This is 2 bug in one related to https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/pull/17141

## Issue Summary
The service depot has now cells you can pass through but not stop or idle. there is 2 way where unit can stop and idle on those cells.

1) Unit idle and become uncontrollable on those cells when a unit is under repair
2) Unit can stop and idle on those cell after an attack order and a stop order

## Reproduction
1)
![bug cell](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28893854/78158837-080db100-7442-11ea-92dd-6163bda4477a.gif)
a) Send several tanks to repair
b) Be sure to be broke so the repair never ends
c) Once a tank is under repair, 2 other tanks will come and block 2 cells they should not waiting their turn
d) Try to control those two tanks independently, they don't respond to move command
e) if you select all the tank including the one under repair, you can "unlock" them.

2)
![bug cell2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28893854/78158887-1a87ea80-7442-11ea-915e-bb13f6c74ee1.gif)
a) Send several tanks to repair or just move across the sd
b) while they are entering/passing through the sd, issue a force fire order
c) Issue a stop order
d) tank will stop and idle on cell they should not



## Expected behavior
they should stay out of those cells or leave them asap


both issues are minor, if it can't be fixed before the release it is not problem as it is very circumstantial.
comments:
Initially, I don't think the tanks are actually idle, the are currently in the `Approaching` state but can't complete their moves into the service depo because it becomes occupied when they are on the transit only tiles. Problem A is that there is no logic here to dictate that they need to move to a stoppable cell, the `MoveAdjacentTo` move type doesn't appear to implement it because it is not necessarily a stopping move.

~~I believe the logic that causes them to stick is because something (possibly `ReturnToCellActivity.Cancel`) expects moving on the spot to shift the Actor to a valid position, which it won't. `ReturnToCell` is also non-interruptible, which might explain why it fails to stop, although I've not stepped through a reproduced example yet.~~ I'm now more certain that this is all `Move` and `MoveAdjacentTo` having states where they can't progress due to the SD being full, but the `Move` can't be cancelled either because the tank isn't on a cell it can stay on. Moving the tank on the SD fixes the lock.

I think the more general problem here is the implementation of transit-only tiles is as as a "parent activity concern" rather than a move-level property. Any activity which does a move that thinks it might be a stopping move needs to additionally consider that, when cancelled, it shouldn't stop on a transit only tile. Really, if this is going to be tight, the move should know whether or not it is allowed to stop on the given tile.

I'd suggest we need some way for a move to know what is coming next, basically whether or not it can actually stop on a `CanStayInCell` tile. At the very least, if the move is going to be cancelled, it needs to check that its final position is a valid stopping cell.

In the second case, I just don't think that the cancel logic is bulletproof for `Move`, it works by clearing the current path, but only if `CanStayOnCell` is true for its current position. If `MoveAdjacentTo` or similar is also used for moving into firing range, the tank can have its destination set to a transit-only tile, so when the path is cleared, there's nothing to tell the unit to move off of the current cell. I think perhaps an expectation is that when it enters idle it checks again? But then again, I think there's an issue here with it getting stuck in one of these positions and unable to be freed.

It sounds like major surgery may be needed to fix this. We should instead consider reverting the service depot / Resupply footprint changes as a lower risk solution for the release.

It sounds like #17849 and the TS bibs are fine because they are never targets for docking orders?
@tovl do you have any thoughts on simpler solutions here?

I think the general problem here is that `Move` could fail to cancel if the target is on a transit only space, and might be solvable by some extra logic to ensure it doesn't get stuck if the path is blocked or that if it ends on a transit only space due to a cancelled "dynamic" move order, it moves the unit off of it.

![Screenshot 2020-04-07 at 21 08 46](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1878992/78714618-195c2f00-7914-11ea-8a72-801fd31e41c1.png)
![Screenshot 2020-04-07 at 21 08 59](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1878992/78714628-1c571f80-7914-11ea-87f3-d5bba2e3a23e.png)

First issue is reproducible with only 2 tanks. Ensure both are damaged. Send one to the SD, and at any time before or after it arrives, send the other. It will get stuck attempting to enter the SD and be unable to move. Issue is that `PopPath` will never gives us an alternative cell, so it's stuck trying to cancel the move when it can't (the first part of `Tick` doesn't allow it to cancel if it's on a transit space, but there's no other code path that would return true in the situation).

@tovl 
> The best way to make sure units won't want to wait for their turn on the repair pad in those cells in the first place is to actually implement the concept of waiting for their turn, i.e. to implement reservation logic for repair pads.

This matches the logic I'm familiar with in RA2, not sure about RA. It's definitely a better solution but the idea that certain moves can stop on a transit-only cell is still a potential problem (easy to do with force-fire).

RE: your solution. I like it but here's an alternative that's more complete but might be do-able: Maybe some logic could also be added to `Move` that scans the path ahead if the next tiles are transit-only? In the case that the exit is blocked, it can select a nearby valid tile to wait on until it becomes unblocked, rather than just stopping. It's effectively an extension to the current blocking detection and waiting, and would (should) cover all move types that might not otherwise respect transit-only tiles. Would also mean the OnIdle logic wouldn't be required.

In case 1, the tank would realise that it can't get to the resource depot that it wants to and wait before entering the transit-only tiles, or if it was currently on the tile then it would move off first.

In case 2, the tank would evaluate its path over the transit-tile, rather than only onto it, so it would have a path to continue following when the move order is cancelled due to being in range to attack. In any other case where the tank would end up on the tile, at least cancelling the move order would work.

IMO the desired behaviour here should be that `MoveAdjacentTo` behaves the same way if surrounded entirely by transit-only cells as it does when surrounded by unpathable cells. In both cases the unit is not allowed to end up in those places.
Well in that case the logic for `Resupply` should probably be reworked not to use it, since SD is the building with transit-only cells.
The checks are made on the cells surrounding the SD, not the SD cells themselves!
@adammitchelldev did you still want to try and put together a PR to fix this?

> @adammitchelldev did you still want to try and put together a PR to fix this?

Yeah, sure, will do that.

> The checks are made on the cells surrounding the SD, not the SD cells themselves!

@pchote Are we sure this is true? I need to look into it harder but if this was the case, surely this bug wouldn't happen because the transit tiles would count as part of the footprint?

review_comments:
I really don't like the idea of this change - I would be willing to bet that this will create more cases where units end up sitting on transit-only tiles or in tunnels, rather than less.

`Move` is often queued as a child activity, and may be cancelled by the parent activity without the unit going idle, meaning that the change in `OnBecomingIdle` won't be able to move the unit out of the cell.

How do you suggest the locking situation be resolved then? The problem occurs when the destination is not reachable due to being blocked, but the current tile is transit-only and therefore refuses to cancel.

I wanted to do this by adding a check-forwards when crossing transit-only to block/re-route if the exit is not currently clear, and being able to catch the case and allow the order to cancel even if it is on a transit-only space when there is no appropriate exit appears to be necessary too.

The main issue I'd see with the change as proposed is that it wouldn't stop a unit deploying on a transit-only space unless they explicitly disallowed it.

We're unlikely to have any proper fix here until we implement more of the long planned docking logic. The simplest workaround would still be to revert the service depots back to a blocking footprint type.

Otherwise, the next simplest workaround that may have to be good enough will be to add some additional logic around the `// HACK` and `// TODO` comments in `Resupply` to make mobile units for do a `MoveAdjacentTo` and then only `MoveWithinRange` / `MoveTo` if they are on an adjacent cell and the target cell is not occupied.

be4a1a59c1dffb539646fbb60d30dc8b02695bde illustrates a way we could implement this for Resupply without regressing other cases. It is a fairly awful hack, but no worse than the rest of the Resupply code.

I'll have a look into doing the "proper" fix tomorrow. Basically having a secondary path pointer to the "exit cell" when you are going over transit only, so that when you `PopPath`, you check both the next cell and the cell you are planning to exit on.
